result.title: A Hard Background Pairing Transfers across Classifiers and Images
result.summary: An image classifier names the object in an image, and its accuracy is the share of images named correctly. A classifier that names a car on a road may miss the same car pasted onto clouds. Composite benchmarks measure such failures by pasting objects cut from photographs onto backgrounds from other photographs. A pairing puts every object label on a different background label, such as truck on sea. The pairing on which some classifiers do worst, their hardest pairing, makes a strict test, but may be hard only for them or only on the photographs used to choose it. We show that the hardest pairing of some classifiers stays hard for others and on new photographs. We split 40 ImageNet classifiers into halves balanced by reported ImageNet accuracy. One half picks its hardest pairing of 8 object and 8 background labels from Common Objects in Context (COCO). The other half, held out of the choice, compares that pairing with random pairings of the same objects and backgrounds. For the 14 held-out classifiers with little net accuracy change after pasting objects back onto their own backgrounds, mean accuracy on composites from new photographs falls from 50.3% over random pairings to 43.7% on the hardest pairing, 6.6 percentage points lower. A benchmark using these composites can compare this pool's held-out classifiers on the fixed and random pairings.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究图像分类器在「物体贴到异类背景」合成的复合图像上的失效，检验某一半分类器选出的最难「物体—背景」配对能否迁移到留出分类器与新照片上，发现准确率仍显著下降。
AI.relevance_reason: 背景捷径导致的物体识别失败，可供核查是否能用作探测 VLM 视觉推理中「是否依赖上下文而非任务必要视觉证据」的诊断范式，但论文本身不涉及 latent 状态、推理过程或 VLM，迁移性尚待确认。
